subject: MAP: stress evaluation results and close plan for embeddings + reranker
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Eva Martinez <eva@searchscale.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff + proposed perf test plan for embeddings + reranker

Eva — thanks again for the time today. Per our MAP (mutual action plan) we promised a focused performance validation for the embeddings + reranker route so you can sign off on latency and throughput before procurement.

Attached: redwood-map-test-plan.pdf (high-level MAP + perf test matrix).

High-level ask: run a controlled stress across your representative query mix, then validate:
- Latency (P50/P90/P99) for embeddings-only endpoint and for reranker endpoint (full candidate scoring).
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) for reranker responses (important for UX).
- Throughput at target concurrencies (25/50/100 concurrent request clients).
- Observed CPU/GPU utilization and token/sec on our dedicated pool.

Proposed schedule:
1) Sep 1 — share test plan (attached) and load script.
2) Sep 2 — Redwood runs two stress passes (50 min each) + one long soak (2h).
3) Sep 3 — share results and recommended tuning; finalize MAP tasks for procurement/PO.

Please confirm the test payload (we recommended ~2k queries representative of your weekly spike) and that procurement is looped in for PO timeline. If procurement needs a specific format for latency/uptime SLAs, flag it now.

Thanks — I cc'd engineering to run the tests and produce the raw logs.

— Karthik Iyer

Thanks Karthik — plan looks good. Procurement is on copy. We can provide the production query sample (2,100 queries) and a candidate pool size distribution for the reranker (avg 12 candidates, 95% <= 20).

A couple quick constraints from our side:
- We want the soak run to include a short holiday-weekend traffic pattern (10% higher short burst).
- Our client-side timeout for the UI is 650ms — anything above that will degrade UX. TTFT is the key metric for the reranker.

I attached the load orchestrator we prefer to use (load-script-v2.py). If you can run exactly that, we can reuse the same baseline later.

— Eva

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Eva Martinez <eva@searchscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-02T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + proposed perf test plan for embeddings + reranker — run results (first pass)

Eva / Karthik — ran the first set of stress passes on Sep 2 using the load-script-v2.py and the 2,100-query sample. Results attached: stress-run-1-results.csv and redwood-stress-summary.pdf. Key outcomes below (test env: Dedicated pool - 4xA10G equivalent, model combo: redwood-embed-1 + redwood-rerank-2b-quant):

Embeddings endpoint (per-request vector generation):
- Concurrency tested: 25 / 50 / 100 clients (clients mean simultaneous connections).
- P50 latency: 34ms / 41ms / 68ms
- P90 latency: 76ms / 92ms / 145ms
- Max sustainable throughput: 2,200 req/s at conc=50 (99% requests complete under 150ms).

Reranker endpoint (candidate scoring flow; includes embedding lookup + cross-scoring):
- Concurrency tested: 25 / 50 / 100
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): 78ms / 112ms / 230ms
- P50 overall latency: 95ms / 140ms / 360ms
- P90 overall latency: 220ms / 315ms / 720ms
- Sustained RPS (full rerank): 380 req/s at conc=50, 160 req/s at conc=100 (noticeable queuing once token buffers exceed GPU memory slice).

Resource observations: GPU utilization peaked ~82% on rerank passes at conc=50, memory headroom reduced at conc=100 triggering small GC-like stalls that explain P99 spikes. Network and host CPU not a bottleneck in our cluster.

Attachments include raw logs + aggregated latency histograms. Next steps: Marissa will provide tuning options (batching window, kv-cache sizing, and quantization profile) that can improve P90/P99 for reranker under conc=100.

— Sean
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Eva Martinez <eva@searchscale.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-02T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — analysis + recommended tuning

Thanks for the dataset and runs — quick analysis and recommended config changes that should fit your production profile:

Summary of recommended tuning (non-disruptive):
- Increase batching window to 12ms for reranker-only shards: reduces P90 by ~18% at conc=50 with negligible P50 impact.
- Enable prefix KV caching for session flows (your queries show ~42% prefix reuse): reduces rerank work per request by ~12% on average.
- Use mixed int8/float16 quant profile for the reranker model (redwood-rerank-2b-quant-opt): drops single-inference memory by ~22%, which eliminates the small memory-driven stalls at conc=100 in our tests.

Revised numbers after applying recommended tuning (simulation run):
Reranker at conc=50 (post-tuning):
- TTFT: 70ms (vs 112ms pre-tune)
- P50: 84ms (vs 140ms)
- P90: 175ms (vs 315ms)
- Sustained RPS: ~460 req/s without queuing

Reranker at conc=100 (post-tuning):
- TTFT: 120ms (vs 230ms)
- P50: 190ms (vs 360ms)
- P90: 420ms (vs 720ms)
- Sustained RPS: ~300 req/s before memory pressure begins to impact P99

Notes / tradeoffs: some minimal model quantization can yield the biggest ops win with small quality delta; we'll include eval prompts from your MAP testset to validate score stability before you sign off.

I'll prepare a short A/B eval pack that runs the same queries through the quantized variant and the baseline; we can attach that to the procurement packet.

— Marissa Cole
Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the clear runbook and the tuned numbers — this is very helpful. Two follow-ups before procurement will sign the PO:
1) Please add the A/B eval results comparing baseline vs quantized reranker on our sample (we need max 1% quality drift on NDCG@10).
2) Can you provide an SLA note for P50/P90 guarantees at our committed conc=50 level and a fallback policy (model variant fallback) in case of cluster-wide contention?

Procurement: our target to issue PO is Sep 15, pending the A/B eval and a short procurement review. If those items are green we can meet that date.

— Eva
